sentences.text: The only known species of this genus is Luskhan itilensis, which was first described in 2017.
The holotype skeleton measures 6.5 meters in length.
It possessed a lower jaw that was 1.59 meters long, leading to an elongated skull with a narrow snout.
The animal had 14 cervical vertebrae, a number intermediate between those of Pliosaurus and Brachauchenius.
Its front flipper bones, the ulna and radius, were very small and roughly the same size as its hind flipper tarsus.
Unlike other pliosaurids, Luskhan lacked an epipodial foramen, a hole in the wrist bones where the ulna and radius meet.
Luskhan convergently evolved traits similar to the distantly related polycotylids, despite their lineages diverging over 10 million years ago.
Analyses show Luskhan is the most polycotylid-like pliosaurid based on skull traits, though its body plan differs.
The holotype specimen was discovered in 2002 by Gleb N. Uspensky near Slantsevy Rudnik in the Ulyanovsk region of western Russia.
The species was formally described in a paper published in Current Biology on June 5, 2017, by Fischer et al.
The genus name Luskhan combines Mongolian and Turkic words for water spirits with the suffix for chief.
The species name itilensis means of the Volga River, referencing the ancient Turkic name for the river.
Ecological analysis suggests Luskhan likely preyed on small, soft-bodied animals, as its slender snout and long symphysis imply a diet of soft prey like fish and squid.
Luskhan independently evolved to occupy a lower trophic level 10 million years after polycotylids did.
It is debated whether serrations and weakly trihedral teeth in Luskhan are functional or vestigial traits retained from ancestors.
Luskhan is classified as an early-diverging brachauchenine within the subfamily Brachaucheninae and the family Pliosauridae.
Phylogenetic analyses vary, but Luskhan is often considered the next most basal brachauchenine after Makhaira.

Luskhan lived during the Lower Cretaceous period in western Russia, specifically during the upper Hauterivian epoch approximately 128 million years ago, with a time range between 132.6 and 125.77 million years ago.

There is a debate regarding whether including Stenorhynchosaurus in the Brachaucheninae clade requires redefining the group, with describers of Stenorhynchosaurus arguing for redefinition while the describers of Luskhan did not.
